key_insight: A unified deep learning pipeline can jointly cancel narrowband interference in OFDM and produce calibrated soft demodulation, avoiding the mismatch that causes error floors in classical receivers.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces sequential processing latency and improves receiver robustness, making it attractive for practical OFDM systems operating under strong or structured interference.
method: NBI-CNet: physics-informed CNN that estimates and removes multi-tone narrowband interference in one forward pass.
LLR-CNet: learns to transform post-cancellation residuals into reliable log-likelihood ratios for decoding.
Scale-invariant design generalizes across FFT sizes without retraining.
evidence_signal: Simulations report up to 60% lower complexity than EOMP-IDS, elimination of baseline error floors, and performance within 0.2 to 0.5 dB of the optimal iterative method at BLER = 10^-4 under SIR = -10 dB.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the trained model matches the interference/channel conditions, so deployment may require validation across the intended signal and spectral-overlap regimes.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Joint Narrowband Interference Cancellation and Soft Demodulation in OFDM Systems
